text:
incident-bot: Pager: api-gateway 502 spike detected in us-west-2 — error rate 18% over 5m, top source: inference-gateway. Paging oncall @sara.

sara: seeing 502s from /v1/generate and streaming endpoints. Spikes across both edge and gateway. Dashboard pinging high latency too.

raj: digging into gateway logs now, lots of upstream 504/timeout errors hitting runtime pods. KV cache hit ratio dropping. P95 backend latency up from 120ms -> 2.3s.

mike: I'm oncall rotation — starting mitigation: will enable edge circuit-breaker, shift some traffic to eu-west-1, and scale down heavy model variants.

alina: CS here — we already have 6 incoming tickets flagged Sev1 from major accounts. Notifying account owners, prepping incident banner.

sara: quick repro: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` returns 502 with body "upstream read timeout". snippet from gateway: ```upstream read timeout\nhost: runtime-03\nresp_time=3.2s\nupstream_status=504\n```

raj: ran `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide`: runtime-quantized-large pods in CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled in dmesg with GPU memory allocation failures during model load. Likely memory pressure on a few nodes.

mike: mitigation steps I'm applying now: 
1) `kubectl scale deploy runtime-quantized-large --replicas=0 -n inference` to remove heavy variant from pool
2) enable fallback routing to smaller-quantized model: `runtime-router set-fallback --from=quantized-large --to=quantized-medium --percent=100`
3) `trafficctl route update inference-gateway --shift eu-west-1=20%` to relieve us-west-2
Doing these sequentially and watching metrics.

sara: applying the traffic shift: `trafficctl route update inference-gateway --shift eu-west-1=20%` — canary started.

incident-bot: Eng escalation: ENG-SRE will be pinged in 5m if error rate remains >10%.

jamie: product/comms: prepping status page text and customer email draft. Share link when ready.

mike: edge circuit-breaker enabled (cfg: `edge.cb.failures=50, window=10s`). Initial metric: errors down to ~9% after 90s. Still seeing tail 504s from a couple runtime nodes.

raj: traced one offending host: runtime-03 showing prefix cache growth during long prompts. Looks like prefix entries not being evicted — mem pressure + OOM. Suggest flushing prefix cache on affected nodes and add eviction policy.

sara: before flush — what's the command?

raj: `redis-cli -h cache-01 KEYS prefix:* | xargs -r redis-cli -h cache-01 DEL` (we should be careful). Alternative: restart cache pods gracefully.

mike: going to restart cache replica-2 gracefully: `kubectl rollout restart sts cache-replica-2 -n inference` — will notify if any regression.

alina: CS update: sent initial customer messages to top impacted accounts, offered mitigation steps and ETA ~30-60m.

incident-bot: Metrics update: error rate 4% over 5m after traffic shift + CB + cache restart. Logging this as mitigated for now.

sara: keeping smaller-model fallback active for 1h, setting alert to watch error rate and p95 latency. Will hand off to night oncall @mike for monitoring. Leaving notes: removed quantized-large from rotation, cache restart done, traffic shift 20% -> eu-west-1.

mike: ack — will monitor and keep status page updates rolling. If error rate climbs >8% re-escalate.

jamie: status page draft: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors impacting us-west-2 API traffic; mitigation in place with partial traffic shift and fallback models. Some customers saw API errors between 14:02-14:18 UTC; we continue to monitor." Link shared: https://status.redwood.dev/incidents/draft/6876543210

alina: logging handoff notes into Zendesk and internal postmortem tracker.

sara: handing off to @mike at 6876543280 — leaving heap & metrics snapshots in the incident doc. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
